We use classification trees to analyze the EEG_128 data set.
EEG_128 has 53 observations, 
1 dependent variable(type) and 
9 independent variables
Add original data to environment
```{r}
EEG <- read.csv("EEG_128.csv")
```


Adjust non-numerical parameters to numerical parameters
```{r}
EEG$gender <- as.factor(EEG$gender)
EEG$type <- as.factor(EEG$type)
```

Start building single trees, and remove the ones that are too perfect
```{r}
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
singletree1 <- rpart(type ~ age + gender + education.years. + PHQ.9 + CTQ.SF + LES + SSRS + GAD.7 + PSQI,
      data = EEG,
      method = "class",
      parms = list(split = "information"),
      control = rpart.control(minsplit = 1))
print(singletree1)
rpart.plot(singletree1)
```
Check for its accuracy
```{r}
y_pred <- predict(singletree1, newdata = EEG, type = "class")

accuracy <- mean(y_pred == EEG$type)
print(accuracy)
```

We remove PHQ.9
```{r}
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
singletree2 <- rpart(type ~ age + gender + education.years. + CTQ.SF + LES + SSRS + GAD.7 + PSQI,
                    data = EEG,
                    method = "class",
                    parms = list(split = "information"),
                    control = rpart.control(minsplit = 1))
print(singletree2)
rpart.plot(singletree2)
```
Check for its accuracy
```{r}
y_pred <- predict(singletree2, newdata = EEG, type = "class")

accuracy <- mean(y_pred == EEG$type)
print(accuracy)
```



Remove GAD.7 and PSQI
```{r}
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
singletree_3 <- rpart(type ~ age + gender + education.years. + CTQ.SF + LES + SSRS,
                    data = EEG,
                    method = "class",
                    parms = list(split = "information"),
                    control = rpart.control(minsplit = 1))
print(singletree_3)
rpart.plot(singletree_3)
```

















In order to properly evaluate the performance of a classification tree on these data, we estimate the test error rather than simply computing the training error. 

We split the observations into a training set and a test set, build the tree using the training set, and evaluate its performance on the test data. 
### Last version: 30 for training and 30 for test 
```{r}
library(caret)
library(rsample)
split <- initial_split(EEG, prop = (nrow(EEG) - 23) / nrow(EEG))
train_data <- training(split)
test_data <- testing(split)
```


Use train data to create a tree
```{r}
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
singletree2 <- rpart(type ~ age + gender + education.years. + CTQ.SF + LES + SSRS + GAD.7 + PSQI,
                    data = train_data,
                      method = "class",
                      parms = list(split = "information"))
print(singletree2)
rpart.plot(singletree2)
```
Use test data to predict and check the accuracy
```{r}
pred <- predict(TrainingTree3, test_data, type = "class")
accuracy <- mean(pred == test_data$type)
print(paste("Accracy:", round(accuracy * 100, 2), "%"))
```
```{r}
Single_Tree <- rpart(type ~ age + gender + education.years. + CTQ.SF + LES + SSRS + GAD.7 + PSQI,
                      data = train_data,
                      method = "class",
                      parms = list(split = "information"))
print(Single_Tree)
```
Use test data to predict and check the accuracy
```{r}
pred <- predict(Single_Tree, test_data, type = "class")
accuracy <- mean(pred == test_data$type)
print(paste("Accracy:", round(accuracy * 100, 2), "%"))
```


```{r}
TrainingTree1 <- rpart(type ~ age + gender + education.years. + PHQ.9 + CTQ.SF + LES + SSRS + GAD.7 + PSQI,
                      data = train_data,
                      method = "class",
                      parms = list(split = "information"),
                      control = rpart.control(minsplit = 1, cp = 0.001))
print(TrainingTree1)
rpart.plot(TrainingTree1)
```
Use test data to predict and check the accuracy
```{r}
pred <- predict(TrainingTree1, test_data, type = "class")
accuracy <- mean(pred == test_data$type)
print(paste("Accracy:", round(accuracy * 100, 2), "%"))
```











Pruning:
Next, we consider whether pruning the tree might lead to improved classification performance. 
We first split the data into a training and test set.
We can use the split before.
We use cross-validation to prune the tree on the training set, 
and then evaluate the performance of the pruned tree on the test set.

Use the previous splitted data before
Train the decision tree(tree2)
```{r}
library(rpart)    # Decision Tree Model
library(caret)    # Accuracy (confusionMatrix)
clf <- rpart(type ~ age + gender + education.years. + CTQ.SF + LES + SSRS + PSQI,
             data = train_data, 
             parms = list(split = "information"),
             control = rpart.control(minsplit = 1))
print(clf)
rpart.plot(clf)
```
Test unpruned tree's accuracy
```{r}
pred <- predict(clf, test_data, type = "class")
accuracy <- mean(pred == test_data$type)
print(paste("Accracy:", round(accuracy * 100, 2), "%"))
```

Next we use the cost_complexity_pruning_path() method of clf to extract cost-complexity values
cost_complexity_pruning_path() is the method in Python,
here in R we use printcp
```{r}
printcp(clf)
```
xerror can be used to select the best pruning point.
We select the CP with the least xerror

Prune the tree
```{r}
pruned_clf1 <- prune(clf, cp <- 0.045455)
print(pruned_clf1)
rpart.plot(pruned_clf1)
```










Use test data to predict and check the accuracy
```{r}
prune_pred <- predict(pruned_clf1, test_data, type = "class")
accuracy <- mean(prune_pred == test_data$type)
print(paste("Accracy:", round(accuracy * 100, 2), "%"))
```
### Random Forest
```{r}
library(caret)
library(rsample)
split <- initial_split(EEG, prop = (nrow(EEG) - 23) / nrow(EEG))
train_data <- training(split)
test_data <- testing(split)
train_variable <- train_data[, -1]
test_variable <- test_data[, -1]
train_type <- train_data[, 1]
test_type <- test_data[, 1]
```

```{r}
library(randomForest)
rf_EEG <- randomForest(x = train_variable, 
                       y = train_type, 
                       mtry = 3, 
                       importance = TRUE) 
print(rf_EEG)  

pred <- predict(rf_EEG, test_variable, type = "class")
accuracy <- mean(pred == test_type)
print(paste("Accracy:", round(accuracy * 100, 2), "%"))
```

```{r}
Random_Forest <- randomForest(train_type ~ . - PHQ.9,
                              data = train_variable,
                              mtry = 3,
                              importance = TRUE) 
print(Random_Forest)
pred <- predict(Random_Forest, test_variable, type = "class")
accuracy <- mean(pred == test_type)
print(paste("Accracy:", round(accuracy * 100, 2), "%"))
```
